newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares drop, market seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares drop, market seen steady.

text.p: Cyprus shares dropped 0.86 percent on Wednesday but the market is expected to remain steady over the next few days, analysts said.
"Political developments are rather fluid at the moment so nobody can be sure where the market is going," said Stelios Markoulis of Laiki Investments.
Marcoulis said politics was the main force behind trends of the market at the moment.
"...I see steady movement of the market over the next few days, we won't have anything spectacular provided there is nothing spectacular on the political front," he said.

The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index, set at 100 points, closed at 76.82 during Wednesday's trading, dropping 0.86 percent during the day and slightly lower than Friday's close of 76.99. Markoulis put the PE ratio of the market at around 16.
Banking stocks closed at 87.83 points from 87.73 on Friday.
The closing price for Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares was 327.5 cents, unchanged from Friday's trading and seemingly unaffected by the banks' 1996 preliminary results released on Friday.

The bank announced net profit gains in 1996 of 5.4 percent. The bank, whose profits rose a record 30 percent in 1995, reported net profits of 24.2 million Cyprus pounds compared with 23 million in 1995.

Popular Bank, which is due to announce its own preliminary 1996 results on Friday, moving its news conference forward one day. Its fully paid shares were trading at 316.5, gaining half a cent on Friday's close. The Hellenic Bank HBCP.CY gained 1.5 cent, closing at 268.5, while the Universal Savings Bank dropped two cents to 165 on its fully paid shares.
Universal Life Insurance shares were trading at 404, recording gains of 1.5 cents. Paneuropean lost one cent to close at 106.5 and Interamerican Insurance dropped four cents to 95 cents.
Vassiliko Cement was up five cents, closing at 143.5, while beer and wine manufacturers Keo was trading at 99.5 down four cents from last week.
Retailers Woolworth was trading at 74.5 cents, dropping 2.5 cents.
